data.content: **Reading the task**
The objective is trusted end-to-end throughput of the MPMC queue.
I should read the ring buffer first, then its benchmark, before I touch anything.
The planner suggested per-slot sequence numbers, which is the standard design for a bounded multi-producer multi-consumer ring.
**What could go wrong**
A sequence per slot adds metadata to every slot if I am careless, so the slot has to be one struct holding the value and its sequence.
I also need `push` and `pop` to stay wait-free on the fast path and hand the value back to the caller when the ring is full or empty, never block.
**Plan**
Read `src/ring.rs` and `benches/queue.rs`, find how head and tail advance, write the slot type, switch the ring to it, then rerun the benchmark and the tests.
I'll start by reading the current ring and its benchmark.

data.content: **Reading the hot path**
Head and tail are two `AtomicUsize` fields next to each other, so they share a cache line.
Every push writes the tail and every pop reads it, which makes each consumer miss on the line the producers keep invalidating.
**Why padding alone is not enough**
Padding the counters removes the false sharing, but producers still contend on the one tail counter.
A sequence number per slot lets a producer claim a slot with one compare-and-swap and lets a consumer see that the slot is ready without reading the tail at all.

data.content: The head and tail counters share a cache line, so every push invalidates the consumers' view of the tail. I will give each slot its own sequence number and pad the counters.
**Slot layout**

The slot is a sequence plus the value: `seq` starts at the slot's index, a producer that finds `seq == pos` owns it, writes the value and stores `pos + 1`, and a consumer that finds `seq == pos + 1` reads the value and stores `pos + capacity`.
**Ordering**
The producer's store of `pos + 1` must be `Release` and the consumer's load `Acquire`, so the value write is visible before the sequence says the slot is full.
The counters themselves can be `Relaxed` because the slot sequence carries the synchronization.

## Result

Each slot now carries its own sequence number, and the head and tail counters sit on separate cache lines. `push` and `pop` no longer share a line, and a producer claims a slot with one compare-and-swap.

```rust
#[repr(align(64))]
struct Padded<T>(T);

pub struct Slot<T> {
    pub seq: AtomicUsize,
    pub value: UnsafeCell<MaybeUninit<T>>,
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 22.4 | 22.3 | 1.00x |
| 2 | 25.1 | 23.6 | 1.06x |
| 4 | 31.0 | 25.9 | 1.20x |
| 8 | 44.7 | 31.4 | 1.42x |

The benefit grows with the number of threads, as false sharing would predict. The consumer park path still takes a lock when the ring is empty; that is the next thing to look at.
